mainTopic: Mixtures with a forbidden item: whether a lost item can be assumed to be the forbidden one, and whether a double doubt (ספק ספיקא) of עבודה זרה is permitted
overview: The גמרא tries to prove from רבי אליעזר's ruling about the heads of mixed-up עולות that slaughtered offerings caught in a mixture can become fit again. It pushes the proof away: רבי אליעזר follows חנן המצרי, who holds that slaughtered animals are never permanently rejected. Next comes רב's rule that if a ring of עבודה זרה is mixed with a hundred rings and one falls into the sea, we assume the lost one was the forbidden one. רבא challenges this, and רב נחמן answers that רב follows רבי אליעזר. Like רבי אליעזר, רב permits the rings only two at a time. רב then rules about a mixture of rings that split into forty and sixty, and the גמרא rereads him: the whole group of sixty, as the majority, carries the איסור. שמואל objects that with עבודה זרה even a ספק ספיקא stays forbidden forever. This leads to a dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, and the גמרא concludes that שמואל follows רבי יהודה only for עבודה זרה. The amud ends by quoting רבי שמעון's 'from ten thousand to three' case again, to examine it on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof from רבי אליעזר about the heads of burnt offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה where רבי אליעזר says that if one head from a mixture was offered, all the other heads may be offered. This seems to show that slaughtered offerings pushed aside by a mixture can become fit again.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learned in a משנה: רבי אליעזר says: if the head of one of them was offered on the מזבח, all the heads should be offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה as a proof. It is trying to show that slaughtered offerings that were pushed aside because they were mixed up do not stay rejected forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that משנה, parts of good עולות got mixed with parts of blemished ones. רבי אליעזר says that once one head was offered, we assume it was the bad one, so the rest are now fine to offer. The offerings were already slaughtered, and they were blocked because of the mixture, yet they become fit again. That suggests slaughtered animals are not permanently rejected (דחוי).

phrases.english: And we learned: Rabbi Eliezer says:
phrases.notes: This משנה comes later in this פרק, about parts of good עולות mixed with parts of blemished ones.

phrases.aramaic: אִם קָרַב הָרֹאשׁ שֶׁל אֶחָד מֵהֶן –
phrases.english: If the head of one of them was offered,
all the heads should be offered!
phrases.notes: The idea is that we assume the head already offered was the blemished one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion about whether slaughtered offerings become permanently rejected (דחויין) because of a mixture. The proof from רבי אליעזר is aimed against the view of רבא that slaughtered offerings caught in a mixture are rejected.
steps.raayaObject: That slaughtered offerings pushed aside because of a mixture are not permanently rejected
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of רבי אליעזר: if one head was offered, all the heads should be offered

steps.title: רבי אליעזר follows חנן המצרי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. רבי אליעזר holds like חנן המצרי, who says that even slaughtered animals are never permanently rejected. The other תנאים disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: He says this following the view of חנן המצרי. As we learned in a ברייתא: חנן המצרי says: even if the blood is already in the cup, the כהן brings another goat and pairs it with this one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof. רבי אליעזר's ruling only fits the view of חנן המצרי, and that is not everyone's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור, two goats are paired: one for ה׳ and one for עזאזל. חנן המצרי says that even after the first goat was slaughtered and its blood is in the cup, if the other goat dies, a new goat can be paired with it. So for him, a slaughtered animal is never rejected. רבי אליעזר's proof therefore only works for those who hold like חנן המצרי.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood already collected in the cup, meaning the animal was already slaughtered
Pairs it up (as the partner goat)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean רבי אליעזר's ruling is wrong. The גמרא is only saying that his ruling depends on a specific opinion, so it cannot prove the point for everyone.

phrases.english: He says it in accordance with Hanan the Egyptian;
as it is taught: Hanan the Egyptian says:
phrases.notes: He is talking about the two goats of יום כיפור, where the goat for עזאזל died.

phrases.english: Even if the blood is in the cup,
he brings another one and pairs it with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 1 by limiting רבי אליעזר's ruling to one opinion.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the proof to the view of חנן המצרי and does not prove anything for the other תנאים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes רבי אליעזר speaks for everyone, but he follows the lone view that slaughtered animals are never rejected
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from רבי אליעזר fails because he holds like חנן המצרי: even slaughtered animals are never permanently rejected.

steps.title: רב: a lost ring is assumed to be the forbidden one
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that if a ring of עבודה זרה gets mixed with one hundred rings and one falls into the sea, all the rest are permitted, because we assume the forbidden one fell.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה in the name of רב: a ring of עבודה זרה that got mixed with one hundred rings, and one of them fell into the Great Sea, all of them become permitted, because we say that the one that fell is the forbidden one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רב about a mixture where one item gets lost. This opens a related topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something forbidden for benefit, like an item of עבודה זרה, is not cancelled even by a majority. Still, רב says that once one ring is lost forever in the sea, we may assume it was the forbidden ring, and all the remaining rings are permitted. This is the same kind of thinking as רבי אליעזר's head that was offered.

keyTerms.meaning: Idol worship. Its items are forbidden for any benefit.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Nahman said that Rabba bar Avuh said that Rav said:
A ring of idol worship
that got mixed with one hundred rings,
and one of them fell into the Great Sea,
all of them are permitted;
for we say: that one which fell is the forbidden one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related rule that uses the same idea as רבי אליעזר: we assume the item that is gone was the forbidden one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When one item from a mixture with a forbidden item is lost forever, we assume it was the forbidden one, and the rest are permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general rule for mixtures of things forbidden for benefit. The next step will test it.

steps.title: רבא challenges רב from animals that must all die
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן from the משנה that says offerings mixed with forbidden animals must all die, even at one in ten thousand. Using רב's logic, once one animal dies, we should say it was the forbidden one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged רב נחמן: the משנה says even one in ten thousand, they must all die. Why? Let us say that the one that died was the forbidden one!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב's rule using a משנה. If the lost item can be assumed to be the forbidden one, the animals in that משנה should not all need to die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that when offerings get mixed with animals forbidden for benefit, all of them are left to die, even if there is only one forbidden animal among ten thousand. With רב's logic, as soon as the first animal dies, we should assume it was the forbidden one and permit the rest. The משנה does not say this, so it seems to go against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: They must be left to die

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection to Rav Nahman:
Even one in ten thousand,
phrases.notes: This is from the משנה at the start of this פרק, about offerings mixed with animals forbidden for benefit.

phrases.english: they must all die.
Why? Let us say:
the one that died, the forbidden one died!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule of רב from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that a lost item from a mixture is assumed to be the forbidden one
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires all the animals to die even when one has already died. This shows we do not assume the lost one was the forbidden one, which goes against רב.

steps.title: רב's ruling follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that רב's ruling about the rings follows רבי אליעזר, not the other תנאים of that משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to רבא: רב, who gave that ruling, holds like רבי אליעזר. As we learned in a משנה, רבי אליעזר says: if the head of one of them was offered, all the remaining heads may be offered.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא's question. He admits that רב's idea of 'we assume the forbidden one is the one that is gone' does not fit the regular opinion, but it does fit רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא asked why the animals in the משנה must all die if we can assume the dead one was the forbidden one. רב נחמן's answer is that the משנה follows the other תנאים, while רב follows רבי אליעזר, who uses exactly this kind of reasoning. So רב's ruling is not wrong; it simply sides with one opinion in a מחלוקת.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב נחמן answering רבא.

phrases.english: Rav, who said this, holds like Rabbi Eliezer;
as we learned, Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם קָרַב הָרֹאשׁ שֶׁל אֶחָד מֵהֶן –
phrases.english: If the head of one of them was offered,
all of the heads may be offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַב דְּאָמַר – כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from step 4 by placing רב's ruling inside the מחלוקת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ruling to one side of a מחלוקת תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's reasoning seemed to clash with the משנה that says all the animals must die.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב follows רבי אליעזר, who does use the reasoning that the missing item was the forbidden one.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר allowed it only two at a time
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges again: רבי אלעזר said that רבי אליעזר allowed the heads only when offered in pairs, not one at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי אלעזר said: רבי אליעזר permitted it only two at a time, but one at a time, no!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's answer. Even רבי אליעזר did not give a full היתר, so how can רב permit the rings without any limit?
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אלעזר, רבי אליעזר only allowed the heads to be offered two at a time, so that at least one head in each pair is surely kosher. Offering them one at a time is not allowed, because that one might be the forbidden head. So רבי אליעזר does not fully rely on 'the missing one was the forbidden one,' and רב's open-ended היתר for the rings seems to go too far.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the names: רבי אלעזר (with an ע) is the אמורא reporting the limit. רבי אליעזר (with an י) is the תנא of the משנה.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Elazar say:
Rabbi Eliezer did not permit
except two at a time,
phrases.notes: In a pair, at least one head is definitely kosher.

phrases.english: but one at a time, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 5 by limiting רבי אליעזר's היתר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that רב's היתר for the rings follows רבי אליעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר only allowed pairs, where one item is surely kosher. רב seems to allow each ring even by itself, which goes further than רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: רב also means two at a time
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that he too only meant that the rings are permitted two at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am also saying two at a time.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא very briefly. רב's היתר for the rings has the same limit as רבי אליעזר's היתר for the heads.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן does not argue with רבי אלעזר. He accepts the limit and applies it to the rings: they may be used or sold only in pairs, so that at least one ring in each pair is surely not the עבודה זרה. With this, רב's ruling fits רבי אליעזר's view exactly.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's היתר for the rings follows רבי אליעזר, and like him it works only two at a time, never one by one.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I too am saying two.
phrases.notes: He means the rings are permitted only two at a time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by accepting the 'two at a time' limit for רב's ruling too.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב seemed to permit each ring even by itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב permits the rings only in pairs, just like רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: A forbidden ring mixed in a hundred that split into forty and sixty
steps.stepSummary: רב rules about a ring of עבודה זרה mixed with one hundred rings that split into groups of forty and sixty. One ring from the forty does not make things forbidden, but one from the sixty does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: a ring of עבודה זרה got mixed into one hundred rings. Forty of them went to one place and sixty to another place. If one ring separated from the forty, it does not make things forbidden. If one separated from the sixty, it does make things forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling of רב about mixed rings. Here the mixture split into two groups, forty and sixty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב treats the groups differently. One ring that left the forty does not cause any איסור, but one ring that left the sixty does. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא asks why a single ring from the sixty should be treated differently.

phrases.english: Rav said:
A ring of idol worship
that got mixed into one hundred rings,
and forty separated to one place
and sixty to another place;
if one separated from the forty, it does not make things forbidden,
one from the sixty does make things forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: טַבַּעַת שֶׁל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבָה בְּמֵאָה טַבָּעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new, related ruling of רב about mixed rings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a mixture split into forty and sixty, a ring leaving the forty does not forbid, while a ring leaving the sixty does.

steps.title: Why should a single ring from the sixty be different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the forty don't forbid because the forbidden ring is assumed to be in the majority, then one ring from the sixty should not forbid either, since the forbidden ring is still assumed to be in the remaining majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about one ring from the forty, that it does not forbid? Because we say the forbidden ring is in the majority. With one ring from the sixty too, we should say the forbidden ring is in the majority!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's ruling as it was just stated. The same reason that lets the ring from the forty go free should also let a single ring from the sixty go free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ring from the forty is permitted because of רוב: the forbidden ring is assumed to be in the bigger group of sixty. But if one ring leaves the sixty, the other fifty-nine are still the majority, so we should assume the forbidden ring stayed with them. So a single ring leaving either group should be permitted.

phrases.english: What is different about one from the forty, that it does not forbid?
Because we say the forbidden one is in the majority;
one from the sixty as well,
we should say the forbidden one is in the majority!
phrases.notes: Here the majority is the fifty-nine rings that are left behind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the internal logic of רב's ruling in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that one ring from the sixty forbids
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רוב reasoning that frees the ring from the forty should also free a single ring from the sixty, because the remaining fifty-nine are still a majority.

steps.title: Rereading רב: the whole group of forty or sixty moved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רב's statement as talking about the whole group moving. All forty moving to one place do not forbid, but all sixty moving to one place do.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what רב said: if all forty separated to one place, they do not make things forbidden. If the sixty went to one place, they do make things forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the challenge by explaining רב differently. He was talking about entire groups moving, not single rings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the new reading, the logic is simple. Because of רוב, the forbidden ring is assumed to be among the sixty. So if all forty get mixed into other rings, those rings stay permitted. If all sixty get mixed in, they bring the assumed איסור with them and forbid the other rings.
steps.whatToRemember: When a mixture splits into two groups, רוב tells us the forbidden item is in the bigger group. That whole group forbids what it mixes into, and the smaller group does not.

phrases.english: Rather, if all forty separated
to one place, they do not make things forbidden,
if the sixty went to one place, they do make things forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִם פֵּרְשׁוּ אַרְבָּעִים כּוּלָּן לְמָקוֹם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by rereading רב's case as entire groups moving.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב was talking about a single ring leaving each group.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב was talking about the whole group of forty or sixty moving. The sixty, as the majority, carry the איסור.

steps.title: שמואל says עבודה זרה stays forbidden even through many doubts
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports that when he told רב's ring ruling to שמואל, שמואל said the ruling does not apply to עבודה זרה, because its doubt and even its double doubt stay forbidden forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I said this ruling in front of שמואל, he told me: Leave עבודה זרה out of it, because its doubt and its doubt-of-a-doubt are forbidden until the end of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה, who reported רב's ruling about the rings, tells us how שמואל reacted to it. שמואל holds that with עבודה זרה, no amount of doubt ever makes things permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said that when the group of forty moves, it does not spread the prohibition, because we assume the forbidden ring stayed with the majority. שמואל disagrees for עבודה זרה specifically, because that prohibition is so strict that even a ספק ספיקא stays forbidden. So according to שמואל, the forty would also be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave aside, do not apply here
A doubt of its doubt (a double doubt)
Until the end of the world, meaning forever

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not arguing about the math of majorities in general. He is saying that עבודה זרה is a special case where the usual leniency for doubts does not work.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main question of the rest of the section: is a double doubt of עבודה זרה forbidden or permitted?

phrases.english: When I said it in front of Shmuel,
phrases.notes: The speaker is רב יהודה, who reported רב's ring ruling from step 8. 'It' means that ruling.

phrases.english: he said to me: Leave aside idol worship,
for its doubt and its doubt of a doubt
are forbidden until the end of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אַמְרִיתַהּ קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, אָמַר לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: שמואל limits רב's ruling from steps 8–10. It does not apply to עבודה זרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With עבודה זרה, both a single doubt and a double doubt remain forbidden forever.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a double doubt of עבודה זרה is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל from a ברייתא. A cup of עבודה זרה forbids a storeroom of cups, but once one cup moves into ten thousand, and one from there moves into another ten thousand, they are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: A doubt of עבודה זרה is forbidden, but a doubt of its doubt is permitted. How so? If a cup of עבודה זרה fell into a storeroom full of cups, they are all forbidden. If one of them moved into ten thousand cups, and from there one moved into another ten thousand, they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the exact opposite of שמואל. It teaches that a double doubt of עבודה זרה is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the storeroom, every cup might be the forbidden one, so that is a single doubt and all are forbidden. A cup that left the storeroom is only maybe forbidden. When one cup then moves from its new group, it is a doubt on top of a doubt, and the ברייתא permits it. This directly contradicts שמואל's claim that a ספק ספיקא of עבודה זרה is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Separated, moved away from the group

phrases.english: They challenged:
A doubt of idol worship is forbidden,
but its doubt of a doubt is permitted.
How so?
A cup of idol worship
that fell into a storeroom full of cups:
all of them are forbidden.
If one of them separated into ten thousand,
and from the ten thousand into ten thousand,
phrases.notes: He means one cup from that second group moved into yet another group of ten thousand.

phrases.english: they are permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's statement in step 11 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a ספק ספיקא of עבודה זרה is forbidden forever.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly permits a double doubt of a cup of עבודה זרה, which contradicts שמואל.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים: רבי יהודה forbids even a double doubt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that תנאים argue about this. רבי יהודה says רימוני באדן forbid in any amount, even when one moves from ten thousand to another ten thousand. That fits שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute of תנאים. As it was taught: רבי יהודה says: Pomegranates of באדן forbid in any amount. How so? If one of them fell into ten thousand, and from that ten thousand one fell into another ten thousand, they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by saying he follows one side of an argument between תנאים. The ברייתא that was just quoted follows the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה forbids a double doubt with רימוני באדן: one pomegranate goes from ten thousand into another ten thousand, and all are still forbidden. שמואל follows this strict view. So the ברייתא in step 12 is not a disproof of שמואל, because it is just the opposing opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
Pomegranates of באדן, a place known for important pomegranates

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic way the גמרא answers a challenge to an אמורא: his view follows one תנא, even if another ברייתא disagrees.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of Tannaim;
as it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Pomegranates of Badan
phrases.notes: These are forbidden pomegranates that are considered too important to cancel out in a mixture.

phrases.english: forbid in any amount.
How so?
If one of them fell into ten thousand,
and from the ten thousand into ten thousand,
they are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 by showing that שמואל follows a different תנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Tannaitic dispute: the challenging ברייתא reflects only one opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא about the cup seemed to be the only view, which would disprove שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה forbids a double doubt, and שמואל follows him.

steps.title: רבי שמעון permits once the doubt spreads further
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא continues with רבי שמעון. He agrees that a pomegranate in ten thousand forbids all of them. But if one moves from there into three, and one of the three moves elsewhere, it is permitted. This is the opinion the cup ברייתא follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: If it fell into ten thousand, they are forbidden. But if one moved from the ten thousand into three, and from the three to another place, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא to show the other side of the argument. רבי שמעון is lenient once there are several levels of doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון agrees with רבי יהודה about the first mixture, so all ten thousand are forbidden. He disagrees once the doubt spreads through more steps, and then he permits. This lenient view matches the cup ברייתא from step 12, which completes the proof that this is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל (a double doubt of עבודה זרה is forbidden forever) follows רבי יהודה. The cup ברייתא (a double doubt is permitted) follows רבי שמעון.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
Into ten thousand, they are forbidden;
but from the ten thousand into three,
and from the three to another place, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 13 by giving the opposing, lenient view.
steps.raayaObject: That the question of a double doubt is truly argued between תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The continuation of the same ברייתא: רבי שמעון's lenient view, set against רבי יהודה's strict view.

steps.title: Whose opinion does שמואל follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא שמואל follows. Neither רבי יהודה nor רבי שמעון seems to fit him.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל, who said this: whose view does he follow? If רבי יהודה, then even other איסורים should be forbidden! If רבי שמעון, then even עבודה זרה should be permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which of the two תנאים from the last steps שמואל agrees with. It shows that neither one fits him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה forbids a double doubt for every איסור, but שמואל forbids it only for עבודה זרה. רבי שמעון permits a double doubt for every איסור, but שמואל forbids it for עבודה זרה. So שמואל seems to stand in the middle, with no תנא behind him.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with whom? Whose opinion does this follow?
Other prohibitions, meaning everything besides עבודה זרה

phrases.english: Shmuel, who said this, follows whom?
phrases.notes: This is שמואל's rule from step 11: with עבודה זרה, even a double doubt stays forbidden.

phrases.english: If he follows Rabbi Yehuda,
then even with other prohibitions it should be forbidden!
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה said his ruling about a forbidden pomegranate, not about עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: If he follows Rabbi Shimon,
then even with idol worship it should also be permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the two opinions brought in steps 13-14 to test שמואל's position.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that only עבודה זרה stays forbidden even in a double doubt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: רבי יהודה is stricter than שמואל, because he forbids all איסורים. רבי שמעון is more lenient than שמואל, because he permits even עבודה זרה. Neither one matches שמואל's split.

steps.title: Blocking the idea that רבי שמעון splits between עבודה זרה and other איסורים
steps.stepSummary: Suppose we say that רבי שמעון himself treats עבודה זרה more strictly. Then the cup ברייתא, which permits a double doubt of עבודה זרה, would match neither תנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say רבי שמעון does make a difference between עבודה זרה and other איסורים, then the ברייתא that says 'a doubt of עבודה זרה is forbidden, but its double doubt is permitted' follows whom? Neither רבי יהודה nor רבי שמעון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a possible way out and then knocks it down. Maybe שמואל follows רבי שמעון, if רבי שמעון is strict only about עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי שמעון forbids a double doubt of עבודה זרה, then the cup ברייתא from step 12 loses its author. That ברייתא permits a double doubt of עבודה זרה. רבי יהודה forbids it, and now רבי שמעון would forbid it too.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (the גמרא brings up a possible answer before rejecting it)
A doubt on top of a doubt, a double doubt

steps.confusionAlert: Read this step together with step 15. It is not a new topic. It closes the one escape route that might have let שמואל fit רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: And if you would say
that for Rabbi Shimon there is a difference
between idol worship and other prohibitions,
then that which was taught in a baraita:
a doubt of idol worship is forbidden,
but its double doubt is permitted,
whose opinion is it?

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן!
phrases.english: It is neither Rabbi Yehuda nor Rabbi Shimon!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא שָׁאנֵי לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects a possible answer to the קשיא of step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי שמעון forbids a double doubt only for עבודה זרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If so, the cup ברייתא, which permits a double doubt of עבודה זרה, would have no תנא to follow.

steps.title: שמואל agrees with רבי יהודה on one point and disagrees on another
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא really follows רבי שמעון. שמואל takes רבי יהודה's strictness for עבודה זרה, but not for other איסורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the ברייתא is רבי שמעון. And שמואל holds like רבי יהודה in one point and argues with him in one point.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 15. שמואל does not have to follow a single תנא completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון stays fully lenient, and the cup ברייתא follows him. שמואל agrees with רבי יהודה that a double doubt of עבודה זרה is forbidden. He disagrees with him about other איסורים, where he permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth (the original idea stands)

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's rule mixes two views. He follows רבי יהודה's strictness, but only for עבודה זרה. The cup ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, who permits a double doubt everywhere.

phrases.english: Really, the baraita follows Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּחֲדָא,
phrases.english: and Shmuel holds like Rabbi Yehuda in one matter,
phrases.notes: The one matter is עבודה זרה, where even a double doubt stays forbidden.

phrases.english: and disagrees with him in one matter.
phrases.notes: The other matter is other איסורים, where שמואל is not strict.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיות of steps 15 and 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Partial agreement: an אמורא may follow one תנא on one point and not on another.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל must follow one תנא completely, so he has no source.
steps.terutzMaskana: The cup ברייתא follows רבי שמעון. שמואל follows רבי יהודה only for עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Quoting רבי שמעון's 'from ten thousand to three' ruling again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's line from the ברייתא again to start looking at it closely.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: if one moves from ten thousand to three, and one of the three moves to another place, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא of step 14 again. It is setting up a closer look at this line, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is ruled here yet. The גמרא picks out רבי שמעון's case: one from the ten thousand falls into three, then one of the three moves elsewhere. That case is now the topic of the next discussion.

phrases.english: The Master said: if one moves from the ten thousand into three,
phrases.notes: 'The Master' is רבי שמעון בן יהודה, quoting רבי שמעון, whose ruling we saw back in step 14.

phrases.english: and one of the three moves to another place, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the שמואל discussion ends, the גמרא goes back to the ברייתא of step 14 to look at its wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, once one moves from ten thousand to three, and one of the three moves elsewhere, it is permitted.
